verdict.rationale: LiveKit ships its own testing tools: pytest/Vitest behavioral tests, LLM-driven agent simulations, and a built-in test framework with judges. A hands-on probe also confirmed that `livekit-server --dev` boots a local development-mode server with placeholder keys and no account, which is a real isolated environment rather than a dry-run. However, nothing in the pack explicitly documents a sandbox that is guaranteed separate from production data or production rooms and telephony. missing for 10: documented sandbox/staging environment with explicit production-data isolation, guidance on isolating tool or API calls during tests, independent corroboration of tests running isolated from production.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: Agent simulations run end-to-end conversations between your agent and an LLM-driven user, then evaluate the results across the full interaction.
Behavioral tests verify specific interactions and expected outcomes. They integrate with your existing test suite using pytest (Python) or Vitest (Node.js)
Builtin test framework: Write tests and use judges to ensure your agent is performing as expected.
